scenario: Multi-area enterprise office: several VLANs, servers, internet, isolation.
prompt:
Background: Northwind Trading is a 45-person wholesale company moving into a single-floor unit. We have four functional groups: sales (18 desktop PCs plus 4 docked laptops), warehouse (about 12 people who use wired terminals), finance (about 8 people, wired PCs that hold our accounting system), and a reception/meeting area (about 7 shared PCs and guest-facing kiosks).

Current environment: nothing — this is a green-field unit, we are pulling one fibre handoff from the ISP.

Target environment:
- Sales, warehouse and finance must each be on their own network. Finance especially must not be reachable by anyone outside finance.
- Reception/meeting PCs and the kiosks are shared and untrusted, so keep them apart from the working groups.
- We need one internal server hosting our intranet (HTTP) that sales and warehouse can open, and a company DNS server.
- Everyone gets addresses automatically, except finance — the finance machines use static addresses.

Constraints / exclusions:
- No wireless for now; wired only.
- No guest internet kiosk isolation magic — just keep them on their own segment.
- Don't add a firewall appliance; our ISP handles the edge.
Priority: get the four segments right first; internet second (we'll add it after the segments are signed off).

requirements.statement: Sales, warehouse, finance and reception are four separate networks
Finance is unreachable from any other group
An internal HTTP intranet server is reachable by sales and warehouse
Finance hosts are statically addressed; everyone else uses DHCP
No wireless and no firewall appliance

expected_behaviour: Four VLANs (sales/warehouse/finance/reception), servers on the sales VLAN, finance machines static while everyone else is DHCP, connected routing, no internet and no firewall (both explicitly excluded).
why_valuable: True L5 long-document: multi-paragraph, four groups, mixed addressing, explicit exclusions, and a priority ordering. Forces full-document extraction; the 'no internet / no firewall' exclusions trap a model that only reads the first line.
